analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 807-1217 and 1218-1601). The patch ranges visible in file_changes (head 453-473, 3239-3242, 3255-3286) fall outside these excerpts, so the displayed text is mostly unchanged surrounding context and the changed cluster-onboarding stop text was not visible in a numbered unit. This is a documentation-only change: no executable code, configuration, keys, or authorization paths are modified, so no concrete security regression can be cited from the supplied text.

Relevant statements in the surrounding documentation were checked against the threat model. Nemotron Super prefix reuse is partitioned by a coordinator-authenticated cache scope and is off without one (lines ~974-983, 1336-1337). That is consistent with T-041's account-scoped salt and mitigation. Durable SSD checkpoints are described as encrypted under the provider cache root (1341-1344). They are bound to the pinned artifact aggregate and the prompt-contract identity (1337-1339, 1357-1362). A post-load hash mismatch is refused. Image checkpoints have no durable layout (1366). None of this loosens the T-041 TTL, HMAC naming, or KEK-purge posture.

Media admission (video decode allowance, charge reservation, 40 MiB body bound, 429/503 refusals) is described as bounded and fail-closed, which is consistent with the availability concerns in TB-007. Remaining questions for later passes: whether the PR's actual code changes (cluster stop counting and the stopsAsked reply field, per the patch excerpt, which was truncated) alter any trust-boundary behavior. Those code files were not in this batch, so the doc claims about the stop logic cannot be verified here. Marking deeper review as not required for the units seen, because no security-relevant behavior change is evidenced.
